text:
Lawson Crouse is Utah's alternate captain and its enforcer of the moment: he dropped the gloves with Simon Benoit after Benoit's hit on Logan Cooley earlier this month. The scoring hasn't followed. He has one goal and five points in 18 games after a 24-goal season, and nothing in his last ten games but two assists.

The goals should come. One goal on 3.5 expected is a shooting percentage of 3.7%, against roughly 13.6% for him, and Utah takes 59% of the expected goals at five on five when he's on the ice. That's a player doing the work and getting nothing for it. Evolving-Hockey had him at 1.4 wins above replacement last season, almost all from even-strength offense, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking found a surprising signature for a big power forward: 18% of his setups came across the royal road, the side-to-side pass through the slot, against 7% for a typical forward. Our range has him around 14 goals by April. That means a lot of them are still to come.
